title: Robots That Walk and Talk Are Coming To Car Factories - Slashdot

content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from The New York Times: At a BMW factory in South Carolina, a human-shaped robot with a screen for a face recently stepped from a charging station toward a stack of green plastic boxes. It grasped an auto part from one of the boxes, pivoted, placed the part in a trolley, then pulled the trolley across the floor. The robot's slow, stiff movements suggested a worker with a bad hangover rather than a technological revolution. "They're still slower than humans," Ulrich Wieland, a BMW vice president in charge of logistics at the factory, in Spartanburg, told reporters invited to see the robot in June. But, he added, "they're advancing fast."

Automakers have used robots for decades, but they are usually powerful, one-armed machines that are fixed in place and perform repetitive tasks like welding body frames or applying adhesives to door panels. Now, most major automakers are betting that robots designed to resemble human beings, known as humanoids, will usher in a new wave of automation and efficiency. Equipped with artificial intelligence, they are expected to move around and do tasks now done by humans without any modifications to factories or heavy equipment.

Unlike most of the robots now in use, humanoids would respond to voice commands and theoretically solve problems and react to unforeseen events. They would never take a lunch break, join a union or require health insurance. To optimists, robots could rescue U.S. manufacturing by increasing productivity, solving shortages of skilled workers and giving Western carmakers a fighting chance at competing with Chinese rivals that enjoy lower costs. Boring but important jobs like sorting parts would be done by robots, freeing humans for more interesting and specialized work.

sentences.zh: 一位匿名读者援引《纽约时报》的报道：在南卡罗来纳州的一家宝马工厂，一个带有面部屏幕的人形机器人最近从充电站走向一堆绿色塑料盒。

sentences.en: It grasped an auto part from one of the boxes, pivoted, placed the part in a trolley, then pulled the trolley across the floor.
sentences.zh: 它从一个盒子里抓起一个汽车零件，旋转，将零件放入手推车中，然后将手推车拉过地板。

sentences.en: The robot's slow, stiff movements suggested a worker with a bad hangover rather than a technological revolution.
sentences.zh: 机器人缓慢而僵硬的动作表明工人宿醉严重，而不是技术革命。

sentences.en: "They're still slower than humans," Ulrich Wieland, a BMW vice president in charge of logistics at the factory, in Spartanburg, told reporters invited to see the robot in June.
sentences.zh: “它们仍然比人类慢，”宝马斯帕坦堡工厂负责物流的副总裁乌尔里希·维兰德（Ulrich Wieland）告诉受邀参观机器人的记者。
但是，他补充道，“他们进展很快。”

sentences.en: Automakers have used robots for decades, but they are usually powerful, one-armed machines that are fixed in place and perform repetitive tasks like welding body frames or applying adhesives to door panels.
sentences.zh: 汽车制造商已经使用机器人数十年，但它们通常是功能强大的单臂机器，固定在适当的位置并执行重复性任务，例如焊接车身框架或在门板上涂粘合剂。

sentences.en: Now, most major automakers are betting that robots designed to resemble human beings, known as humanoids, will usher in a new wave of automation and efficiency.
sentences.zh: 现在，大多数主要汽车制造商都押注，设计得与人类相似的机器人（称为类人机器人）将迎来新一轮自动化和效率浪潮。

sentences.en: Equipped with artificial intelligence, they are expected to move around and do tasks now done by humans without any modifications to factories or heavy equipment.
sentences.zh: 配备人工智能后，它们有望四处走动并完成现在由人类完成的任务，而无需对工厂或重型设备进行任何修改。

sentences.en: Unlike most of the robots now in use, humanoids would respond to voice commands and theoretically solve problems and react to unforeseen events.
sentences.zh: 与现在使用的大多数机器人不同，类人机器人会响应语音命令，理论上可以解决问题并对不可预见的事件做出反应。

sentences.en: They would never take a lunch break, join a union or require health insurance.
sentences.zh: 他们永远不会午休、加入工会或需要健康保险。

sentences.en: To optimists, robots could rescue U.S. manufacturing by increasing productivity, solving shortages of skilled workers and giving Western carmakers a fighting chance at competing with Chinese rivals that enjoy lower costs.
sentences.zh: 对于乐观者来说，机器人可以通过提高生产率、解决技术工人短缺的问题来拯救美国制造业，并为西方汽车制造商提供与成本较低的中国竞争对手竞争的机会。

sentences.en: Boring but important jobs like sorting parts would be done by robots, freeing humans for more interesting and specialized work.
sentences.zh: 像零件分类这样无聊但重要的工作将由机器人完成，从而使人类能够从事更有趣和专业的工作。

content_html_zh: 一位匿名读者援引《纽约时报》的报道：在南卡罗来纳州的一家宝马工厂，一个带有面部屏幕的人形机器人最近从充电站走向一堆绿色塑料盒。 它从一个盒子里抓起一个汽车零件，旋转，将零件放入手推车中，然后将手推车拉过地板。 机器人缓慢而僵硬的动作表明工人宿醉严重，而不是技术革命。 “它们仍然比人类慢，”宝马斯帕坦堡工厂负责物流的副总裁乌尔里希·维兰德（Ulrich Wieland）告诉受邀参观机器人的记者。 但是，他补充道，“他们进展很快。” 汽车制造商已经使用机器人数十年，但它们通常是功能强大的单臂机器，固定在适当的位置并执行重复性任务，例如焊接车身框架或在门板上涂粘合剂。 现在，大多数主要汽车制造商都押注，设计得与人类相似的机器人（称为类人机器人）将迎来新一轮自动化和效率浪潮。 配备人工智能后，它们有望四处走动并完成现在由人类完成的任务，而无需对工厂或重型设备进行任何修改。 与现在使用的大多数机器人不同，类人机器人会响应语音命令，理论上可以解决问题并对不可预见的事件做出反应。 他们永远不会午休、加入工会或需要健康保险。 对于乐观者来说，机器人可以通过提高生产率、解决技术工人短缺的问题来拯救美国制造业，并为西方汽车制造商提供与成本较低的中国竞争对手竞争的机会。 像零件分类这样无聊但重要的工作将由机器人完成，从而使人类能够从事更有趣和专业的工作。
